transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Start time: 14:00 UTC (2:00 PM)
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Horizon Head InfoSec), Tom Bradford (Procurement), Noah Li (Cloud Architect), Maya Singh (Legal)

Summary:
Quick roundtable to align on vendor adoption playbook items: SSO/SAML integration, KMS/privileged keying options, egress cost modeling for private vs hosted, and next steps for legal (DPA/MSA redlines). Goal: decide whether to proceed to a two-week pilot and route pricing approvals.

Topics covered (auto sections may be imperfect):
- Current procurement gating and approver list
- SSO / SAML vs OIDC expectations and SCIM provisioning
- KMS options: customer-managed keys (CMK) via Cloud KMS or HSM + Redwood integrations
- Egress cost sensitivities and billing model (per-token + egress fee)
- DPA redlines, SLA windows, audit logs retention and SOC2 evidence

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: all right hey everyone thanks for joining i think we've got about 50 minutes, um quick intros and then we'll jump right in. i'm lena from Redwood, ae on this account. dan is our infra se.
[00:08] Aisha Khan: thanks lena, hey all, aisha here. quick note we might have to loop in our cloud team later cause of peering.
[00:15] Tom Bradford: tom from procurement, i have the approval calendar so i'll flag timing as we go.
[00:18] Noah Li: noah, cloud architect, i'll be the technical owner for network and keys.
[00:21] Maya Singh: maya, legal counsel, i'll comment on DPA and MSA redlines.
[00:26] Daniel Ortiz: hey team, daniel ortiz, infra SE at redwood; i'll cover KMS and private-deploy options.

[00:34] Lena: cool, so big picture — horizon's asked for clarity on SSO, kms, and costs tied to egress before procurement greenlights. is that a fair summary, tom?
[00:42] Tom: yes, primarily cost predictability and legal alignment. we need to see pricing that won't surprise FinOps.

[00:51] Aisha: and from infosec we need to ensure keys are under our control or strong attestation, plus audit logs retained for six months at minimum.

[00:58] Daniel: understood. we support three main patterns: hosted with Redwood-managed keys (fastest), hosted with customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key), or Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with customer KMS. each has tradeoffs on latency, cost, and egress.

[01:15] Noah: can you just spell out how egress charges show on the invoice? we have a chunk of regulatory traffic that sits in GCP and cross-region egress is expensive.

[01:23] Daniel: yes, so currently for hosted we bill per-token usage plus a regional egress line item if data leaves your cloud. for dedicated/private we can reduce egress by colocating or peering which often moves cost from vendor egress to internal networking — depends on peering and if we can host in your VPC.

[01:36] Aisha: i'm worried about the "if" — our security policy forbids shared keys in some cases. we need to know exact attestation and KMS rotation controls.

[01:44] Daniel: fair. for BYOK we support Cloud KMS integrations (e.g., Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) with envelope encryption — Redwood never persists plaintext model state, and keys are used for encrypting at rest artifacts. rotation and audit logs are surfaced; there is a small HSM integration path if needed (that's the private + HSM flow).

[02:05] Maya: small point on wording in the DPA; the liability paragraph currently says "reasonable efforts" which Procurement flags as vague. we'll propose stronger language and a cap. lena, can you get a redline outline?

[02:14] Lena: yes we'll do an annotated redline. we'll include a one-page summary of the asks so it's easier for your legal.

[02:19] Tom: timeline-wise our pricing committee meets next wednesday; i need a clean cost sketch and the DPA exception list by monday COB ideally.

[02:27] Lena: okay monday cob — noted. daniel, can you surface an egress sketch by then or do you need more time?

[02:33] Daniel: i can do a high-level sketch by monday; for accurate numbers i need token volume estimate and where traffic originates — that's noah's input.

[02:40] Noah: i can provide 3-month baseline token estimate and regions by friday. expect 200k requests/day with a 1.2k token average per request for initial scope, but that's rough.

[02:51] Aisha: also note we have data residency constraints for EU customers — anything touching EU PII must stay in eu-west region and be subject to full audit logging.

[02:58] Daniel: we can pin models to eu-west and enable prefix caching to reduce cross-region egress. there may be a small delta for model repo synchronization but we can outline that.

[03:08] Maya: on SLA, can we confirm uptime window and incident response times? the draft MSA mentions 99.5% monthly uptime but we might ask for 99.9 for critical endpoints.

[03:16] Lena: current standard plan is 99.5 for hosted tier; Dedicated comes with higher SLAs. we can propose an enterprise SLA in the MSA variant; i'll flag options in the redline doc.

[03:26] Tom: cost delta for dedicated — is that committable? procurement wants clear numbers for reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go.

[03:33] Daniel: yes, reserved dedicated pools are a commit with lower per-token unit price and better latency predictability. i'll produce a three-scenario model: hosted (pay-go), dedicated reserved (monthly commit), and private (one-time infra setup + lower egress if peered).

[03:49] Aisha: about SSO: we use PingFederate today, SCIM provisioning is a must. can you support SCIM push for group sync? we can't do manual account creation.

[03:58] Daniel: yes we support SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning for groups and roles is supported in our console. a small caveat: initial role mappings require an admin onboarding step.

[04:09] Noah: network wise we'll need to validate VPC peering, NAT egress and routes. also curious about private link options; we prefer private link over public egress if possible.

[04:20] Daniel: we have private link and VPC peering options. private link reduces public egress routes but there is some setup lead time. i'll document expected network changes and a preflight checklist.

[04:30] Lena: ok i'm hearing the follow: horizon wants — BYOK or HSM attestation, SCIM/SSO, clear egress costing, and MSA/DPA redlines with SLA options. we aim to get procurement and legal signoff to start a two-week pilot. is that right?

[04:40] Tom: yes, and procurement needs a firm-ish number for dedicated commit scenario to take to finance.

[04:45] Maya: legal will push back on indemnity and data residency — we'll provide exact redline language.

[04:50] Daniel: one technical note about KV cache (the transcript incorrectly shows KV cash sometimes) — prefix caching can dramatically reduce token counts and egress on steady-state workloads. i'll include a small benchmark from a similar customer in the spreadsheet.

[05:03] Noah: that would be useful. also please show how quantization or smaller model variants affect costs.

[05:09] Daniel: yes i'll include model variant delta and quantization guidance — tradeoffs on quality vs token efficiency.

[05:18] Lena: quick procurement question — any blockers on your side to sign an SCC or EU addendum if needed?
[05:24] Maya: we may need an EU DPA addendum; i'll confirm the list of countries and send a template.

[05:31] Tom: final timing check: we need pricing + annotated DPA by monday COB, noah sends volumes by friday, pilot preflight to be scheduled next week, and legal will review redlines and propose language by monday as well.

[05:42] Lena: great. we'll also share a short runbook for the pilot and a one-page security summary (SOC2 + audit artifacts). link will be included in the follow-up email.

[05:50] Maya: one last thing on logs — retention 180 days is our starting ask, but we might need longer for specific customers. can you make retention configurable?

[05:57] Daniel: yes retention is configurable; we'll note default and options in the security summary.

[06:03] Lena: awesome. thanks everyone. we'll capture next steps and circulate the DPA redline and cost model. any final questions?
[06:11] Aisha: no, thanks.
[06:12] Tom: none here.
[06:13] Noah: all good.
[06:14] Maya: thanks.

Notes / links referenced:
- DPA draft link: https://redwood.example/dpa-draft (redwood hosted doc)
- Pilot cost template: spreadsheet shared after call
- Security summary: SOC2 & KMS brief (will attach)

End of transcript.

Errors/quality notes: auto-transcription sometimes shows "KV cash" instead of "KV cache"; a few proper nouns (PingFederate, HSM) may have been transcribed inconsistently. There is occasional overlapping talk and filler words retained.
